item.title: How Chemistry and Rocket Motors Constrain American Warfighting
item.description: Solid rocket motors—and the chemicals that fuel them—are a major limitation on America’s missile stockpiles, and one that cannot be solved by additional funding alone. The post How Chemistry and Rocket Motors Constrain American Warfighting appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How America Misread the Iranian Middle Class
item.description: The United States believed that economic pressure would turn Iran’s middle class against the regime. Why hasn’t it? The post How America Misread the Iranian Middle Class appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What Is a Russian Warship Doing in Vietnam?
item.description: Russia’s Marshal Shaposhnikov Udaloy-class destroyer stopped in Vietnam on its way back to Vladivostok, the home base of Russia’s Pacific Fleet. The post What Is a Russian Warship Doing in Vietnam? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Hegseth to Latin America: Help Us Fight the Cartels—or Else
item.description: At the “Americas Counter Cartel Conference” in Miami, Hegseth suggested that the United States would unilaterally pursue military operations in Latin American countries if their governments refused to help. The post Hegseth to Latin America: Help Us Fight the Cartels—or Else appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why the USS Gerald R. Ford Was Perfect for Operation Epic Fury
item.description: The Ford is now stationed in the eastern Mediterranean, but its air wing is well within reach of Iran. The post Why the USS Gerald R. Ford Was Perfect for Operation Epic Fury appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Iran War and the Post-Liberal Global Order
item.description: America’s ongoing military campaign in Iran has dispelled lingering illusions about the “liberal international order”—and laid bare the power politics defining the 21st century. The post The Iran War and the Post-Liberal Global Order appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: America’s “PrSM” Missile Just Made Its Debut in Iran
item.description: The precision-strike missile can be fired from existing M142 HIMARS launchers, but has a range well beyond its usual payload. The post America’s “PrSM” Missile Just Made Its Debut in Iran appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The US Navy Has Shrunk, but the Royal Navy Has Nearly Disappeared
item.description: The Royal Navy—once the pride of the United Kingdom—has shrunk to around two dozen warships, insufficient to project power in any meaningful sense. The post The US Navy Has Shrunk, but the Royal Navy Has Nearly Disappeared appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The IRGC: Understanding America’s Enemy in “Operation Epic Fury”
item.description: The IRGC has been dramatically weakened since the beginning of the Iran conflict last week—but it will be far harder to destroy. The post The IRGC: Understanding America’s Enemy in “Operation Epic Fury” appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How the Iran War Is Upending US Middle East Strategy
item.description: With the demand that Iran give up its ballistic missiles, the United States has made a long-term military commitment to maintaining Israeli missile supremacy. The post How the Iran War Is Upending US Middle East Strategy appeared first on The National Interest.
